domains.name: Artist management
journeys: Artist registers, verifies identity, completes onboarding, saves profile, reloads it, and updates the public press kit.
Manager joins an artist workspace with limited rights, edits permitted profile fields, and loses access after revocation.
Artist uploads profile artwork, replaces it, sees the durable public version, and removes the asset without orphaned storage.
Artist exports or erases account data while contractual and financial retention rules remain explicit.
risks: Deletion that leaves public assets behind

domains.name: Fan management
journeys: Artist imports fan contacts with consent and deduplication, creates a segment, and verifies persisted membership.
Fan opts into a membership, changes preferences, unsubscribes, and stops receiving eligible future messages.
Artist drafts a fan campaign, previews recipient eligibility, schedules a sandbox delivery, and observes genuine delivery failures.
Manager searches, paginates, exports, and deletes authorized fan data without seeing another artist's fans.

domains.name: Project management
journeys: Artist creates a project, assigns a collaborator and tasks, attaches files, changes status, and reloads all durable records.
Collaborator edits an allowed task while a second actor edits concurrently; conflicts are explained without lost updates.
Artist duplicates a project and verifies new ownership and independent assets; deleting a project cleans only its owned resources.
Manager manages project budgets, deadlines, search, filtering, and export across authorized workspaces.

domains.name: DAW studio
journeys: Producer opens a saved session, imports audio, edits tracks and regions, saves, closes, and reopens the same arrangement.
Producer records or creates MIDI, changes tempo, edits markers and automation, and verifies playback timing.
Producer renders or exports a mix, observes progress and cancellation, and retrieves the genuine output asset.
Collaborator lacking edit or export permission is denied; an interrupted save or render resumes without corrupting the session.
risks: Audio clock drift and browser restrictions

domains.name: Content distribution
journeys: Artist creates a release, enters credits and rights, uploads valid masters and artwork, and reviews validation errors.
Artist submits a release through the authorized provider sandbox and tracks genuine pending, accepted, rejected, and retry states.
Artist retries a timed-out submission without duplicate releases, reconciles provider status, and handles signed callbacks.
Artist requests a supported update or takedown and sees explicit provider and contractual constraints.
risks: Partial chunk upload or callback replay

domains.name: Marketing automation
journeys: Artist connects a sandbox channel with least privilege, drafts campaign content, previews it, and schedules delivery in the correct timezone.
Manager reviews an automated proposal, approves only the intended action, and sees the resulting delivery receipt.
Artist pauses or cancels a campaign before execution; workers respect consent, rate limits, and revocation.
Artist inspects attribution and failure metrics and reconnects an expired integration without losing drafts.

domains.name: Revenue analytics
journeys: Artist imports or syncs a royalty statement, maps releases and splits, and reconciles totals to the source.
Manager filters revenue by period, currency, source, and project; the UI distinguishes missing data from zero income.
Artist records refunds or corrections and verifies historical reports, payouts, and exports without double counting.
Collaborator views only entitled royalty shares and disputes a mismatch through a documented workflow.

domains.name: AI assistant
journeys: Artist asks a question grounded in authorized project data and receives a traceable answer or an explicit uncertainty response.
Artist requests an action, reviews the proposed side effects, and sees only authorized tools execute.
A retrieved document or user message tries to override permissions; the assistant keeps tenant data and tool authority isolated.
Artist cancels a generation, reaches a rate or budget limit, or encounters a provider outage and gets a recoverable state.
risks: Tool calls crossing tenant or consent boundaries

domains.name: Collaboration tools
journeys: Artist invites a collaborator, collaborator accepts once, and both see the correct project and role.
Members exchange comments or messages, edit concurrently, reconnect after a network loss, and reconcile durable state.
Owner changes or revokes permissions while a session is active; subsequent reads, writes, and subscriptions enforce the change.
Members review a contribution, resolve a conflict, and access only licensed shared files.

domains.name: Marketplace systems
journeys: Seller creates a licensed listing, uploads assets, previews public metadata, and publishes only a valid listing.
Buyer starts sandbox checkout and receives the checkout session without the platform claiming a paid purchase.
A verified payment event creates one order and one entitlement; repeated callbacks or retries never duplicate revenue or access.
Buyer downloads only entitled assets, requests a supported refund, and seller sees reconciled order and payout status.

domains.name: Subscription management
journeys: User selects a plan, starts sandbox checkout, and receives entitlements only after authoritative payment confirmation.
Subscriber upgrades, downgrades, cancels, or restores an eligible plan with explicit effective dates and proration behavior.
Payment failure, retry, refund, chargeback, or out-of-order webhook updates the subscription once and reconciles stale state.
User inspects invoices and billing history while another tenant cannot access them; disabled providers surface a truthful unavailable state.

domains.name: Administrative controls
journeys: Authorized administrator completes required authentication, opens scoped dashboards, and sees current source-backed status.
Administrator investigates a support or moderation case using least-privilege access and records an attributable action.
Administrator changes a permitted control, previews its impact, and can identify or roll back the change through an audit trail.
Non-admin, revoked admin, and cross-tenant users are denied both UI and direct API access; bulk actions are bounded and idempotent.
risks: Sensitive data in dashboards or logs

templates.title: Inventory the actual repository and execution environment
inputs: Pinned source revision and source digest
Tracked file inventory and package scripts
steps: Record runtime and package-manager versions from actual commands.
Enumerate frontend entrypoints, server entrypoints, shared schemas, workers, and deployment manifests.
Record environment-variable names and service prerequisites without reading values.
Identify owned commands for build, check, tests, startup, and artifact validation.
List absent tooling and blocked capabilities with their effects on verification.
deliverables: Repository and runtime inventory with exact paths
acceptance: Every claimed component has an observed path or command source.
Missing capabilities remain blocked or unverified.
validation: Reviewer traces a sample of each component class to pinned source.
Command availability is distinguished from successful execution.

templates.title: Reconcile mission scope with the existing launch ledger
steps: Apply the user-authorized admin-private release scope; keep all twelve domains usable by the existing administrator and retain public launch items as deferred.
Read the existing launch scope without deleting outstanding items.
List personas, tenants, subscription levels, and supported environments.
Map each requested domain to current journeys and unresolved assumptions.
Define explicit launch-critical outcomes and defer only with recorded product authority.
Record missing decisions as blockers with an owner and the smallest clarification needed.
acceptance: All twelve domains remain represented.
Prior unaccepted pages are not silently accepted by template expansion.
Admin readiness and public readiness are separate explicit decisions; public onboarding and high concurrency cannot block unrelated admin workflow fixes.
validation: Compare catalog journeys and existing ledger identifiers.
Reviewer checks that missing information has a blocker rather than an invented requirement.

templates.title: Build the page-to-service dependency inventory
inputs: Tracked services, schemas, workers, and tests
steps: Enumerate route declarations and dynamic route parameters.
Trace route components through API calls into handlers and storage operations.
Record authentication and subscription gates at each layer.
Link existing tests and observability to each observed route.
Mark untraced edges explicitly and create follow-up discovery work.
acceptance: Every discovered route has an owner and mapped or explicitly unknown dependencies.
A rendered page is not recorded as a completed business workflow.
validation: Sample public, authenticated, and admin routes end to end.
Reconcile counts against route registration rather than directory names.

templates.title: Specify system boundaries and cross-domain invariants
steps: Map service and data ownership across domains.
Define identity, tenancy, assets, payments, and event invariants shared across domains.
Identify transaction and asynchronous handoff boundaries.
Record deployment and scale assumptions with explicit unknowns.
Write decisions for consistency, compatibility, and failure isolation.
acceptance: Every shared entity and side effect has one authoritative owner.
Capacity assumptions are labeled assumptions until measured.
validation: Reviewer follows one upload, payment, and collaboration flow across boundaries.
Contradictions become blocking design tasks.

templates.title: Prioritize complete launch journeys and defect severity
inputs: Current failed and unverified gate report
steps: List the complete actor-to-durable-outcome sequence for each launch journey.
Identify where payment, rights, privacy, or data loss can harm users.
Rank confirmed defects before speculative enhancements.
Record dependency order, user impact, and effort assumptions.
Assign a responsible specialist and a measurable completion check to each priority.
acceptance: No critical path ends at a button click or HTTP 200 without durable outcome evidence.
Severity is supported by a concrete failure or explicit verification need.
validation: Reviewer verifies the highest-priority journeys have positive and negative acceptance scenarios.

templates.title: Audit authentication, session, and account-recovery contracts
steps: Trace registration, login, logout, session renewal, MFA, recovery, and revocation.
Identify cookie, token, CSRF, rate-limit, and redirect handling.
Map sensitive actions requiring reauthentication.
Define expired, stolen, revoked, replayed, and cross-origin test cases.
Record exploitable findings with exact source and reproduction conditions.
acceptance: Every identity transition has success and denial cases.
No secret or live session value appears in the artifact.
validation: Run approved isolated auth checks through the trusted verifier.
Manual analysis remains separate from actual executed evidence.

templates.title: Map tenant isolation and role enforcement
steps: List roles and their read, create, modify, delete, export, and admin capabilities.
Trace tenant derivation from authenticated identity into each store query.
Identify object identifiers accepted from clients and jobs.
Specify horizontal and vertical escalation probes for each resource family.
Map stale role, invitation, and realtime-session invalidation cases.
acceptance: Every resource family has explicit allow and deny rules.
Client-supplied tenant IDs are never assumed authoritative.
validation: Reviewer selects one resource per domain and traces its enforcement.
Trusted tests retain actual denial responses and unchanged-store checks.

templates.title: Inventory persistent data, constraints, and retention
steps: Map entity keys, tenant keys, relationships, nullable fields, and uniqueness constraints.
Identify source-of-truth records versus derived caches and analytics.
Record asset ownership and cascade or cleanup behavior.
List personal, financial, and rights-sensitive fields with retention requirements.
Document existing migrations and rollback constraints.
acceptance: Every critical entity has an authoritative store and ownership key.
Retention and deletion assumptions remain explicit.
validation: Reviewer traces artist, project, order, subscription, and asset lifecycles.
Schema declarations are checked against actual migrations where available.

templates.title: Inventory providers and sandbox acceptance requirements
steps: List provider purpose, API version, required scopes, and callback contract.
Distinguish absent configuration, local fixture, provider sandbox, and production evidence.
Define valid, rejected, rate-limited, expired, and unavailable responses.
Record signed-event, retry, reconciliation, and revocation requirements.
List missing sandbox capabilities without requesting secrets in reports.
acceptance: No provider is marked functional solely because a mock passed.
Every irreversible external action has an explicit execution boundary.
validation: Reviewer traces each configured provider to a real adapter and test source.

templates.title: Define independent verification layers and evidence contracts
inputs: Existing test commands and coverage policy
steps: Map each acceptance criterion to unit, integration, browser, contract, or operational evidence.
Specify disposable services, deterministic fixtures, cleanup, and network boundaries.
Require fresh source-bound raw results and explicit skip counts.
Define old-behavior failure checks for bug regressions.
Preserve existing coverage thresholds and identify uncovered code rather than excluding it.
acceptance: Each release criterion has a producer or a visible unverified blocker.
Mock results are labeled and do not satisfy provider or deployment acceptance.
validation: Reviewer checks schema, command, exit, source hash, and artifact freshness requirements.

templates.title: Diagnose build and CI execution prerequisites
inputs: Observed CI annotations and local command receipts
steps: Separate jobs that never started from actual command failures.
Record account, runner, network, dependency, and resource blockers.
Reproduce owned build and check commands with documented runtime limits.
Compare lockfiles, package scripts, and nested dependency installation requirements.
Prepare a narrow repair proposal without modifying protected workflow or package files automatically.
acceptance: Account billing or missing runners are not represented as code failures.
Configuration edits require the separate review path.
validation: Trusted commands capture actual exits and logs.
Reviewer compares local execution environment with declared CI environment.

templates.title: Verify source-to-artifact provenance and packaging
steps: Identify all generated artifact roots and expected deployment assets.
Inspect how source, dependencies, and environment influence the build.
Run the configured build only through the trusted verification interface.
Validate manifest source binding and required asset hashes.
Record packaging omissions, stale assets, and runtime dependency gaps.
acceptance: Artifact existence alone never passes the gate.
A changed source or artifact invalidates earlier readiness evidence.
validation: Invoke the configured final artifact validator and retain its actual result.
Reviewer checks missing and tampered asset cases.

templates.title: Verify production startup, readiness, and shutdown semantics
steps: Define cold startup prerequisites and dependency failure cases.
Start the packaged production artifact in isolation and observe actual readiness endpoints.
Exercise degraded dependencies and verify readiness is truthful.
Send graceful shutdown signals and inspect draining, cleanup, and exit behavior.
Record startup duration, resource use, logs, and remaining processes.
acceptance: Simulation output cannot satisfy real startup acceptance.
All owned processes and disposable resources are cleaned up.
validation: Trusted harness must retain process lifecycle and health observations.
Missing production-start harness leaves start unverified.

templates.title: Specify logs, metrics, traces, and alert ownership
steps: Define service-level indicators for success, latency, availability, and job age.
Map correlation identifiers across request, transaction, job, and provider boundaries.
Specify log redaction and bounded error metadata.
Define alert thresholds, routing ownership, and actionable runbook links.
Identify missing monitors with exact instrumentation points.
acceptance: No sensitive payload is required for diagnosis.
Each alert has an owner, trigger, and next action.
validation: Reviewer checks a success, denial, provider outage, and worker failure trace.

templates.title: Design and rehearse backup, restore, and rollback evidence
steps: Define recovery objectives and the data required to verify them.
Identify backup creation, integrity, retention, and restoration procedures.
Plan restore into an isolated environment with no production writes.
Verify application consistency and asset references after restoration.
Document deployment and migration rollback limits and reconciliation steps.
deliverables: Recovery drill plan and result references
acceptance: A backup file is not proof of successful restoration.
Unperformed drills remain unverified.
validation: Trusted drill checks restored rows, ownership, assets, and service behavior.
Reviewer verifies recovery time and data-loss claims against observations.

templates.title: Audit application and supply-chain exposure
inputs: Dependency locks and trusted audit command
steps: Run dependency audit through the configured trusted gate.
Inspect risky request parsing, file access, redirects, outbound fetch, and command execution.
Map XSS, CSRF, SSRF, injection, replay, and API-abuse test targets.
Check secrets handling and redaction without printing credential values.
Classify findings by confirmed exploitability and required mitigation.
acceptance: Zero dependency advisories is not equivalent to secure application behavior.
Critical and high unresolved findings block release.
validation: Each confirmed finding retains a safe isolated reproduction.
Reviewer checks false positives and mitigation acceptance.

templates.title: Define accessibility coverage for every critical interaction state
steps: List every form, modal, menu, table, editor, upload, and status interaction.
Specify accessible name, role, label, description, and announcement expectations.
Define keyboard order, focus restoration, zoom, reflow, and reduced-motion checks.
Separate automated checks from assistive-technology and manual observations.
Map uncovered states to explicit accessibility tasks.
acceptance: Route render coverage cannot substitute for state-level accessibility.
Unsupported or untested input modes stay visible.
validation: Reviewer checks keyboard completion of representative artist and admin journeys.

templates.title: Define realistic capacity and responsiveness experiments
inputs: Observed data volumes and product targets
steps: Use measured private-admin workload and real asset sizes first; record massive public concurrency targets as later work.
Specify workload mix, payload sizes, data cardinality, and concurrency increments.
Set an isolated target, resource budget, maximum duration, and abort criteria.
Measure baseline API p95 and page-load distributions with sample counts.
Record query, CPU, memory, queue, and browser traces at saturation.
Separate extrapolated capacity from directly measured capacity.
acceptance: No production or public host is load-tested by this loop.
Claims of scale include workload, environment, duration, and sample count.
validation: Trusted producer supplies fresh api_p95_ms and page_load_seconds values.
Reviewer checks warmup, errors, and measurement bias.

templates.title: Specify agent and model authority boundaries
steps: Enumerate model inputs, retrieved content, tool names, and side effects.
Specify structured outputs and deterministic validation before tool execution.
Map tenant filtering, user confirmation, budget, cancellation, and escalation requirements.
Define prompt-injection and data-exfiltration adversarial cases.
Record unavailable models or tools as blocked capability.
acceptance: Untrusted repository, provider, or retrieved text never grants tool authority.
A model claim never proves a side effect happened.
validation: Reviewer traces one read-only answer and one proposed mutation.
Trusted evaluations retain actual tool calls and denial outcomes.

templates.title: Define truthful product and financial event semantics
inputs: Existing event emitters and aggregate readers
steps: Define unique event identity, actor, tenant, timestamp, and origin.
Separate requested, scheduled, submitted, accepted, paid, refunded, and failed outcomes.
Identify duplication, late arrival, timezone, and currency behavior.
Specify consent, retention, redaction, and access controls.
Map every revenue metric to authoritative financial records.
acceptance: Checkout creation never counts as a paid purchase.
Missing or stale data is distinguishable from a genuine zero.
validation: Reviewer traces one metric backward to its authoritative record.
Trusted tests cover replay and out-of-order events.

templates.title: Map product, API, and operational documentation needs
steps: List user onboarding and task guides required for each domain.
Map API contracts and error behavior to documentation sources.
List setup, testing, recovery, incident, and release runbooks.
Identify examples that disagree with current source.
Record owner, reviewer, and freshness rules for every required document.
acceptance: Unsupported features are not documented as available.
Each launch-critical document has an observed location or explicit gap.
validation: Reviewer follows a setup and a user journey using the draft instructions.

templates.title: Define defect reproduction, triage, and escalation protocol
steps: Specify minimal failure packets with source, command, environment, and raw evidence.
Require a failing invariant and competing root-cause hypotheses.
Define severity, owner, regression test, and rollback criteria.
Set repeated-failure and no-progress escalation rules.
Define how lessons change ordering or prompts without weakening acceptance.
acceptance: Repeated identical failures stop or change investigation strategy.
A narrative root cause without reproduction remains a hypothesis.
validation: Reviewer applies the protocol to one previously observed failure.

templates.title: Expand broad work into exact member assignments
inputs: Domain templates and discovered route matrix
steps: Create an instance for each concrete route, entity, transition, integration, and acceptance scenario in scope.
Bind every instance to exact observed file paths and one accountable role.
List prerequisites, permitted edits, expected artifacts, reviewer, and verification producer.
Split tasks exceeding the time budget or spanning unrelated state transitions.
Keep undiscovered behavior and unresolved source mappings in a visible discovery backlog.
acceptance: Template instantiation is not claimed to enumerate undiscovered behavior.
No task starts without bounded inputs, scope, completion criteria, and ownership.
validation: Reviewer checks one fully expanded journey per domain.
Dependency and path-overlap checks reject conflicting concurrent edits.

templates.title: Review shared contracts before cross-domain integration
inputs: Shared identity, event, and data invariants
steps: Compare field names, versions, errors, and tenant identity across producer and consumer boundaries.
Identify incompatible state transitions and duplicate source-of-truth ownership.
Check event delivery and retry assumptions.
Route contradictions to the exact owning task.
Record accepted contracts and unresolved integration blockers.
acceptance: No contradictory contract is silently selected by the coordinator.
Dependent implementation remains blocked until the contract is accepted.
validation: Reviewer traces producer and consumer behavior for payments, assets, and collaboration.

templates.title: Design fault injection and degraded-operation acceptance
steps: Select controlled database, cache, queue, storage, provider, and network failures.
Define expected timeout, retry, circuit, user message, and recovery behavior.
Set blast-radius, cleanup, and abort limits for each experiment.
Specify durable-state checks after interruption and replay.
Identify faults that cannot be safely reproduced in the current environment.
acceptance: All experiments are confined to disposable resources.
Missing fault capability remains unverified.
validation: Trusted harness records injected fault timing and observed recovery.
Reviewer checks no hidden loss, duplicate side effect, or false success.

templates.title: Compile release gates without converting unknowns into passes
steps: List every required gate with exact source, policy, command, exit, and evidence path.
Separate failed checks, unexecuted checks, provider skips, and invalid stale evidence.
Verify source and artifact identity after all checks.
Record launch-blocking gaps and their accountable specialists.
Prepare a GO or NO-GO recommendation without granting release authority.
acceptance: All required gates must pass; a high score cannot hide a blocker.
Task completion and review prose cannot override verifier output.
validation: Reviewer independently resolves each evidence link and freshness constraint.

templates.title: Prepare the operational and product handoff package
steps: Assemble setup, user, support, API, incident, and recovery references.
State current release decision and outstanding blockers plainly.
List ownership and the next action for each operational alert.
Provide disable and rollback instructions for the loop itself.
Record the exact candidate revision and artifact references for handoff.
acceptance: No deployment or readiness claim exceeds retained evidence.
A new operator can identify how to stop the loop and recover.
validation: Reviewer follows the handoff links and checks command prerequisites.

templates.title: Turn repeated failures into evaluated workflow improvements
steps: Group failures by verified cause rather than message similarity alone.
Compare repair success, regression, latency, and no-progress rates.
Propose a narrower task, better evidence, changed ordering, or improved prompt.
Evaluate the proposal against retained adversarial and regression cases.
Keep failed experiments and never reduce gates or budgets silently.
acceptance: A claimed improvement has a measurable baseline and evaluation.
Runner or policy changes require their own reviewed code change.
validation: Reviewer checks that optimization preserves mandatory gates and review independence.

templates.title: Map privacy requests and data lifecycle evidence
inputs: Export, erasure, consent, and retention routes
steps: Map collection purpose, consent, access, retention, export, and erasure for each personal-data class.
Trace copies in assets, logs, caches, analytics, backups, and providers.
Define identity verification for privacy requests.
Record retention conflicts and legal-policy questions without inventing legal conclusions.
Specify executable export and deletion acceptance scenarios.
acceptance: Technical checks are not represented as GDPR, CCPA, or SOC2 certification.
Every claimed deletion identifies retained exceptions.
validation: Reviewer traces one user export and erasure across stores and providers.

templates.title: Review dependency installation and artifact trust boundaries
steps: Inventory package sources, install hooks, binaries, and nested workspaces.
Check that reproducible installs use the committed locks.
Identify executable content downloaded at build or runtime.
Record provenance gaps and safe remediation proposals.
Validate that generated artifacts do not unexpectedly contain secrets or source-only files.
acceptance: No dependency upgrade is applied blindly by an automatic audit fix.
Protected manifest or lockfile changes follow separate review.
validation: Reviewer compares declared and observed installation paths and build inputs.

templates.title: Define coordinator and worker resource budgets
steps: Set finite task, cycle, elapsed-time, and worker limits.
Define cancellation propagation and cleanup responsibilities.
Schedule only independent work with nonoverlapping edit ownership.
Set memory, disk, command-output, and provider-budget limits for the executor environment.
Specify blocked-capability and no-progress termination outcomes.
acceptance: No unbounded recursion or spawn loop is authorized.
Path checks are described as coordination protections rather than a hostile-code sandbox.
validation: Reviewer tests cancellation, exhaustion, and overlapping-task rejection through runner tests.

templates.title: Build a source-level coverage gap queue
inputs: Fresh coverage summary and file details
steps: Verify coverage source identity, parser completeness, and instrumentation scope.
List uncovered executable branches and functions by file.
Prioritize uncovered authorization, payment, persistence, and failure paths.
Create behavior-focused test proposals rather than line-execution filler.
Keep generated test proposals outside protected existing tests until reviewed integration.
deliverables: Coverage gap queue by source location
acceptance: No source exclusion or threshold reduction is used to improve the score.
Passing tests and coverage attainment are reported separately.
validation: Reviewer checks branch expectations against actual behavior and coverage raw data.

templates.title: Specify bounded detection and remediation runbooks
steps: Map each supported symptom to deterministic evidence and a bounded diagnosis.
Define reversible candidate remedies and their preconditions.
Require isolated validation and regression checks before proposing production action.
Specify stop, escalation, rollback, and repeated-failure behavior.
Document unsupported symptoms and missing monitoring capabilities.
acceptance: This task does not install a production remediation daemon.
A health alert cannot authorize arbitrary code or database mutation.
validation: Reviewer walks a latency, worker crash, and provider outage scenario.

templates.title: Reconcile final discoveries back into the mission ledger
inputs: Exact task ledger and remaining discoveries
steps: Compare completed tasks with every launch requirement and discovered user action.
Reopen requirements whose source changed after acceptance.
Record explicit unsupported paths, untested states, and provider gaps.
Assign new concrete tasks for newly discovered behavior.
Preserve the release NO-GO until all mandatory evidence is current.
acceptance: No task count or percent complete substitutes for feature acceptance.
The discovery backlog cannot be silently dropped at cycle exhaustion.
validation: Reviewer samples accepted and unaccepted requirements against current source and receipts.

templates.title: Trace {domain} from UI action to durable result
steps: Locate the actual routes, components, handlers, services, schemas, jobs, and provider adapters for {domain}.
Trace every declared journey action to its durable state or explicit missing implementation.
List duplicate, legacy, disconnected, and unreachable code paths.
Record permissions, dependencies, and current tests for each path.
Create a gap entry for every unresolved edge instead of guessing a source path.
acceptance: Each claimed implementation has an exact observed path and symbol.
Path hints are discovery aids, not permission or proof.
validation: Reviewer independently follows one complete journey and one denial path.

templates.title: Specify exact {domain} acceptance scenarios
steps: Use the existing administrator as the primary actor and enumerate every admin-visible action, including actions shared with ordinary artist accounts.
Enumerate actor, tenant, preconditions, action, expected state, and visible result for every journey.
Add invalid input, denied role, missing dependency, interrupted operation, and retry outcomes.
Identify irreversible or financial effects and their acceptance requirements.
Separate present behavior from required behavior.
Assign a stable criterion identifier to every scenario.
acceptance: Every scenario has an observable durable outcome and failure expectation.
Unanswered product decisions remain blocking assumptions.
validation: Reviewer rejects vague criteria such as works correctly or page loads.

templates.title: Expand {domain} into bounded concrete work packages
inputs: Criterion identifiers and concrete source map
steps: Split each route, entity, transition, integration, and scenario into separate concrete assignments.
Name exact files, symbols, fixtures, and expected artifact locations.
Assign one owner, a different reviewer, and upstream dependencies.
Bound each work package to the configured time and path scope.
Preserve new discoveries as child work rather than claiming exhaustive coverage.
deliverables: Exact file ownership and handoff map
acceptance: Every implementation package names its acceptance criteria and verification producer.
Unrelated changes are separated even when they share an owner.
validation: Reviewer checks dependency completeness and edit-scope overlap.

templates.title: Define {domain} business state transitions
steps: List valid states and permitted transitions for each domain resource.
Define the actor and precondition required for each transition.
Specify invalid, repeated, concurrent, delayed, and reversed transitions.
Identify authoritative records and transaction boundaries.
Define how UI, jobs, and providers reconcile divergent states.
acceptance: Every transition has an observable success and rejection outcome.
Provider intent is not confused with completed work.
validation: Reviewer traces the domain's highest-risk concurrent or financial transition.

templates.title: Specify {domain} role and tenant access
steps: Enumerate read, create, edit, delete, export, share, and privileged actions.
Define actor-to-resource ownership checks for every action.
Trace direct API, background job, websocket, and download access paths.
Specify revoked access, stale sessions, and cross-tenant identifier probes.
Record missing enforcement as concrete defects.
acceptance: All entrypoints enforce the same ownership invariant.
Hiding a UI control is not authorization.
validation: Reviewer checks one horizontal and one vertical escalation case per resource family.

templates.title: Design {domain} persistence and integrity constraints
steps: Map each required field to type, default, nullability, and ownership.
Specify foreign keys, uniqueness, and transaction constraints.
Define pagination, sorting, time, currency, and retention semantics.
Plan backward-compatible migration and rollback for missing structures.
Record migration proposals outside protected execution until independently reviewed.
acceptance: Business invariants have database or transactional enforcement where appropriate.
No production migration is executed by this task.
validation: Reviewer checks duplicate, orphan, null, boundary, and rollback behavior.

templates.title: Define {domain} request and response contracts
steps: Specify method, path, authenticated actor, request schema, and response schema.
Define validation and domain error codes with stable client meaning.
Bound payload sizes, pagination, filtering, and sorting.
Define idempotency, retry, timeout, and cancellation behavior.
Record compatibility requirements for existing clients and providers.
acceptance: Every mutation defines authorization, validation, and durable success semantics.
Internal errors and sensitive fields are not exposed as public contracts.
validation: Reviewer compares contract to frontend requests and service signatures.

templates.title: Specify every {domain} interaction and recovery state
steps: Map screen entry, navigation, task actions, confirmation, and completion.
Specify loading, empty, validation, denied, failed, partial, and success states.
Define focus movement, keyboard shortcuts, announcements, and responsive layout.
Explain destructive or financial consequences before the action.
Provide recovery steps for interrupted, offline, or unavailable dependencies.
acceptance: Every API failure has a useful visible response.
Success messaging reflects authoritative completion state.
validation: Reviewer walks each journey with keyboard-only and narrow-screen assumptions.

templates.title: Threat-model {domain} assets and side effects
steps: Identify valuable data, assets, privileges, money, and external actions.
Map untrusted input to parsing, storage, rendering, fetching, and tool boundaries.
Define safe isolated attack cases for relevant injection, traversal, replay, and abuse risks.
Prioritize exploitability and impact using source evidence.
Attach a mitigation and verification criterion to every confirmed finding.
acceptance: Speculative concerns are distinguished from reproduced failures.
No public or production target is attacked.
validation: Reviewer checks coverage of all identified trust boundaries.

templates.title: Implement {domain} request validation and truthful errors
inputs: Concrete validation defect and owned file list
Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Locate the earliest trusted request boundary for the selected endpoint.
Validate required fields, types, lengths, ranges, enums, and unknown input.
Normalize only documented safe values and reject ambiguous values.
Map failures to stable client errors without internal details.
Return success only after the promised durable operation has completed.
acceptance: Malformed, oversized, and unauthorized requests do not mutate state.
Error messages identify recoverable user input without leaking data.
validation: Trusted tests cover empty, malformed, boundary, and valid requests.
Independent reviewer inspects actual changed handlers.

templates.title: Implement {domain} authorization at every entrypoint
inputs: Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Derive actor and tenant identity from trusted authentication context.
Check resource ownership and action permission before reads or mutations.
Apply the same rule to jobs, downloads, exports, and realtime entrypoints in scope.
Handle revoked or missing membership deterministically.
Keep denial responses and audit events free of sensitive resource details.
acceptance: Cross-tenant and insufficient-role requests are denied without side effects.
Client-supplied ownership does not override trusted context.
validation: Trusted negative tests assert denied responses and unchanged stores.
Reviewer traces direct API bypass attempts.

templates.title: Implement durable {domain} writes and integrity checks
inputs: Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Replace selected ephemeral or simulated success with the authoritative persistence operation.
Enclose related writes in the appropriate transaction boundary.
Enforce uniqueness, references, ownership, and expected current state.
Return persisted identifiers and values rather than invented client echoes.
Handle rollback and partial failure without orphaned records.
acceptance: Reload and independent read return the promised durable result.
Failed operations do not leave inconsistent records or false success.
validation: Trusted integration tests use actual disposable persistence.
Reviewer inspects transaction and rollback boundaries.

templates.title: Implement replay-safe {domain} mutations
inputs: Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Choose the authoritative operation identity and scope it to the actor and resource.
Enforce duplicate detection atomically at the persistence boundary.
Return consistent results for safe repeated requests.
Reject conflicting reuse and handle interrupted operations explicitly.
Record retry and reconciliation outcomes for diagnosis.
acceptance: Parallel or repeated requests do not duplicate business side effects.
Idempotency is not implemented only in process-local memory.
validation: Trusted tests issue duplicate, concurrent, and interrupted retries.
Reviewer verifies state and side-effect counts.

templates.title: Implement bounded and correct {domain} reads
inputs: Concrete query paths and observed plans
Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Apply ownership filters before pagination and aggregation.
Bound page size and validate stable sorting and cursor semantics.
Avoid fetching entire collections for server-side filtering.
Remove confirmed N+1 access or redundant reads using measured evidence.
Preserve accurate empty, partial, and missing-resource semantics.
deliverables: Before and after query evidence references
acceptance: Pagination is stable and does not leak cross-tenant counts.
Optimizations preserve correctness under changing data.
validation: Trusted tests cover empty sets, page boundaries, ties, and tenant isolation.
Reviewer compares measured query plans where available.

templates.title: Implement safe {domain} asset lifecycle behavior
inputs: Concrete upload, download, replace, and delete paths
Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Validate file size, type, naming, and storage destination at the trusted boundary.
Bind uploaded assets to the authorized owner and operation.
Handle partial upload, cancellation, retries, and cleanup.
Authorize downloads and derived or paid assets independently.
Implement replacement or deletion without removing resources owned elsewhere.
deliverables: Asset lifecycle patch or explicit not-applicable evidence
acceptance: A task may be not applicable only with reviewed source evidence; it cannot silently skip a required journey.
Corrupt, empty, oversized, or unauthorized assets fail safely.
validation: Trusted tests inspect storage and metadata after failures and retries.
Reviewer verifies path traversal and ownership denial.

templates.title: Implement durable {domain} background work
inputs: Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Persist job intent atomically with the triggering business state.
Use bounded retry, timeout, lease, and deduplication semantics.
Record progress, terminal failure, cancellation, and reconciliation.
Recover interrupted or abandoned work without duplicated external effects.
Expose truthful pending and failure states to the API.
deliverables: Background job patch or explicit not-applicable evidence
acceptance: In-memory scheduling does not promise durable completion.
Worker restart and retry preserve business invariants.
validation: Trusted tests interrupt and restart an isolated worker.
Reviewer checks dead-letter and exhausted-retry behavior.

templates.title: Verify the {domain} provider integration contract
steps: Identify exact requests, responses, scopes, callbacks, and supported operations.
Compare adapter assumptions with available authoritative provider documentation or sandbox observations.
Define unavailable, rejected, rate-limited, expired, and partial-success behavior.
Mark fixture-only evidence and missing sandbox capabilities.
Write a concrete compatibility and acceptance contract.
deliverables: Domain provider contract or reviewed no-provider finding
acceptance: No live provider outcome is inferred from fixtures.
Unknown or unsupported operations return explicit limitations.
validation: Reviewer checks each required provider operation against available evidence.

templates.title: Implement truthful and resilient {domain} provider behavior
inputs: Concrete adapter defect and sandbox boundary
Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Validate outbound payload and minimize transmitted data.
Apply bounded timeout, retry, rate-limit, and idempotency behavior.
Parse provider responses and preserve genuine rejection or pending states.
Handle token expiry and revocation without leaking credentials.
Reconcile partial outcomes before retrying irreversible actions.
deliverables: Provider adapter patch or explicit not-applicable evidence
acceptance: Provider outage never yields a fabricated successful action.
Only provisioned sandbox capabilities are exercised.
validation: Trusted contract and sandbox tests record actual provider boundaries.
Reviewer distinguishes mock behavior from provider evidence.

templates.title: Implement authenticated and replay-safe {domain} callbacks
inputs: Callback contract and authoritative state machine
Concrete webhook handler and storage paths
Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Verify signatures and timestamps over the correct raw payload.
Bind callback identity to the correct tenant and provider account.
Persist event identity and apply state transitions atomically.
Handle duplicates, out-of-order delivery, retries, and unknown events.
Return truthful acknowledgements and retain safe reconciliation metadata.
deliverables: Callback handler patch or reviewed no-callback finding
acceptance: Unsigned or mismatched callbacks cannot change state.
Duplicate callbacks do not duplicate orders, revenue, messages, or entitlements.
validation: Trusted tests cover signature failures, replay, ordering, and transaction failure.
Reviewer checks canonical raw-body handling.

templates.title: Implement {domain} route and component behavior
inputs: Concrete frontend file ownership and API contract
Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Connect the selected route and component to the accepted API contract.
Implement semantic layout and clear action labels.
Render loading, empty, denied, failed, partial, and success states.
Preserve navigation and route parameter handling.
Reflect actual server state and make incomplete capabilities explicit.
acceptance: Visible success reflects server-confirmed outcomes.
No required interaction remains a dead or placeholder control.
validation: Trusted browser checks exercise the selected interaction states.
Reviewer compares implementation with the design contract.

templates.title: Implement robust {domain} forms and client validation
inputs: Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Use labeled controls with appropriate input types and constraints.
Keep client validation consistent with server requirements.
Preserve user input across recoverable failures.
Prevent accidental duplicate submission while handling legitimate retry.
Focus and announce the error summary or completed action appropriately.
acceptance: Users can identify and correct each invalid field using keyboard and screen reader semantics.
Client validation never replaces server validation.
validation: Trusted browser tests cover invalid, valid, duplicate, and failed submission.
Reviewer checks focus and accessible error relationships.

templates.title: Implement {domain} state synchronization and cancellation
inputs: Concrete client cache and async paths
Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Define the authoritative cache keys by tenant and resource.
Invalidate or update dependent state only after confirmed outcomes.
Cancel or ignore stale responses during navigation and identity changes.
Handle concurrent edits and offline or reconnect behavior explicitly.
Roll back optimistic state on rejection without hiding the error.
acceptance: Tenant switching never reuses another tenant's cached data.
Stale responses cannot overwrite newer confirmed state.
validation: Trusted tests simulate delayed responses, logout, tenant switch, and failed mutation.
Reviewer checks cache identity and cleanup.

templates.title: Implement authorized {domain} realtime synchronization
inputs: Realtime need and accepted event contract
Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Authenticate and authorize subscription and publication separately.
Bind channels and event payloads to tenant and resource ownership.
Handle revocation, disconnect, heartbeat, and reconnect.
Reconcile missed or duplicate events against durable state.
Bound queues and payloads and expose degraded operation truthfully.
deliverables: Realtime patch or reviewed no-realtime finding
acceptance: A stale connection cannot preserve revoked access.
Realtime delivery is not the sole source of durable state.
validation: Trusted tests cover cross-tenant subscription, revocation, duplicate events, and reconnect.
Reviewer verifies event ordering assumptions.

templates.title: Implement responsive {domain} interactions
inputs: Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Inspect task completion at narrow, tablet, desktop, and wide layouts.
Fix overflow, obscured controls, truncation, and unusable touch targets.
Preserve content order and keyboard access across responsive variants.
Handle zoom and reflow without requiring unnecessary horizontal scrolling.
Check menus, dialogs, tables, and editors in their expanded states.
acceptance: Critical actions remain reachable and comprehensible in every supported layout.
Screenshots alone do not prove interaction success.
validation: Trusted browser checks record viewport and completed task behavior.
Reviewer inspects zoom and touch target evidence.

templates.title: Repair concrete {domain} accessibility violations
inputs: Observed violation with route and state
Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Reproduce the exact keyboard, semantic, contrast, or announcement failure.
Implement the smallest semantic or interaction correction.
Preserve focus, name, role, state, and error relationships.
Check the neighboring loading, empty, and failure states.
Record residual limitations and the exact retest scenario.
acceptance: Each claimed fix corresponds to a reproduced violation.
Automated zero violations does not claim unperformed assistive-technology validation.
validation: Trusted scanner and interaction checks run on the changed state.
Independent accessibility reviewer checks keyboard completion.

templates.title: Instrument meaningful {domain} operational outcomes
inputs: Concrete request, job, and provider paths
Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Add correlation across the selected request, transaction, job, and provider boundary.
Record success, denial, retry, failure, and reconciliation outcomes.
Emit bounded latency and outcome metrics without sensitive payloads.
Ensure failures surface through the documented health or alert signal.
Keep logging and metrics from changing business success semantics.
acceptance: Telemetry failure cannot strand an already completed business result.
Logs avoid secrets and unnecessary personal data.
validation: Trusted tests verify representative signals and failure isolation.
Reviewer checks redaction and cardinality.

templates.title: Implement truthful {domain} product and revenue events
inputs: Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Locate the authoritative event-emission point for the selected outcome.
Emit stable identity and tenant-scoped event metadata.
Separate initiation, pending, completed, paid, refunded, and failed events.
Deduplicate retries and reconcile delayed provider confirmations.
Present missing or stale aggregates honestly in downstream consumers.
acceptance: User-submitted interaction labels cannot forge financial completion.
Analytics failure does not roll back unrelated completed user actions.
validation: Trusted tests compare events and aggregates against authoritative records.
Reviewer checks duplicate, refund, and late-arrival behavior.

templates.title: Specify bounded {domain} AI behavior and evaluations
steps: Identify whether the domain actually invokes models or tools and document evidence.
Define grounded inputs, structured outputs, and uncertainty behavior.
Specify role and tenant filtering before retrieval or tool execution.
List side-effect confirmation, cancellation, budget, and unavailable-provider behavior.
Create domain-specific injection, hallucination, leakage, and task-success evaluations.
deliverables: AI behavior contract or reviewed no-AI finding
acceptance: Absence of AI is justified by traced source rather than assumed.
Model-generated text does not prove actions or authoritative facts.
validation: Reviewer checks one allowed and one adversarial scenario for each tool class.

templates.title: Implement bounded and truthful {domain} AI execution
inputs: Accepted AI contract and evaluation cases
Concrete model, retrieval, and tool paths
Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Validate structured model outputs before consuming them.
Filter retrieval and tool arguments using trusted actor and tenant identity.
Separate untrusted content from system authority and side-effect authorization.
Enforce bounded turns, timeouts, cancellation, and configured budgets.
Return explicit uncertainty or unavailable states when evidence or capability is missing.
deliverables: AI boundary correction patch or reviewed no-AI finding
acceptance: No model output can directly bypass authorization or invoke arbitrary commands.
Unsupported generation is not replaced with fake completed output.
validation: Trusted evaluation harness records actual outputs, tool calls, and denials.
Reviewer checks prompt-injection and cancellation cases.

templates.title: Author independent {domain} business-rule test proposals
inputs: Exact changed symbols and current test gaps
steps: Select observable business rules and failure boundaries in the changed code.
Write deterministic positive, negative, boundary, and state-transition cases.
Avoid assertions that merely mirror implementation details.
Prove a bug regression case fails against the old behavior when available.
Write proposed test artifacts to the private task directory for reviewed integration.
deliverables: Executable unit-test proposals outside protected source
acceptance: Test proposals do not count as executed passing tests.
Existing tests and thresholds remain unchanged.
validation: Independent reviewer checks expected results against requirements.
Trusted verifier executes only separately approved test integration.

templates.title: Author {domain} persistence and API integration test proposals
steps: Specify actual HTTP and persistence boundaries for each case.
Create actor, tenant, entity, and asset fixtures with deterministic cleanup.
Assert durable state after success, denial, rollback, retry, and restart.
Include concurrent mutation and duplicate-side-effect cases.
Write executable proposals and dependency requirements outside protected source.
acceptance: Mock-only tests are labeled and cannot prove real persistence behavior.
Every mutation case asserts resulting state, not only response status.
validation: Reviewer traces assertions to authoritative stores.
Trusted execution retains raw results and cleanup evidence.

templates.title: Author {domain} provider and callback acceptance test proposals
steps: Define contract fixtures for success, rejection, throttling, expiry, and timeout.
Define real sandbox cases separately from controlled local cases.
Cover signature failures, duplicates, ordering, and reconciliation.
Assert only genuine provider-supported outcomes and retained receipts.
Write executable proposals with explicit missing-capability and skip rules.
acceptance: A skipped sandbox case remains unverified.
Live credentials are never placed in artifacts.
validation: Reviewer checks mock and sandbox results cannot be confused.
Trusted verifier reports every skip and missing provider capability.

templates.title: Author {domain} role-based end-to-end journey tests
steps: For each critical persona, start from a realistic logged-in or public state.
Perform real UI actions through the complete journey.
Assert durable outcomes after reload and independent read.
Exercise denied roles, error recovery, interrupted actions, and session expiry.
Write executable browser proposals with stable semantic selectors and cleanup.
acceptance: Page render or button visibility alone cannot satisfy a business journey.
Fixtures do not pre-create the outcome the journey is supposed to produce.
validation: Reviewer follows every acceptance criterion to a concrete assertion.
Trusted execution records browser failures and actual persisted results.

templates.title: Create {domain} boundary and abuse experiments
steps: Prepare empty, malformed, huge, corrupt, duplicate, and unexpected inputs relevant to the domain.
Define unauthorized actor, tenant, and subscription combinations.
Include traversal, replay, concurrency, and prompt-injection cases where applicable.
Set resource and duration bounds and cleanup expectations.
Record exact expected denial and unchanged-state assertions.
acceptance: Experiments target only disposable authorized resources.
Absence of a crash is not proof of correct rejection.
validation: Independent reviewer checks input limits and authoritative-state assertions.
Trusted execution retains actual results, not worker conclusions.

templates.title: Create {domain} concurrency and recovery experiments
steps: Identify simultaneous actions that can conflict over the same resource.
Synchronize requests at the relevant race boundary.
Inject timeout, disconnect, worker crash, and retry during mutation.
Assert uniqueness, ownership, ordering, and final durable state.
Bound request counts and document cleanup and expected recovery.
acceptance: Sequential repetitions are not presented as concurrency evidence.
Every experiment has a known final-state oracle.
validation: Reviewer checks synchronization and fault placement.
Trusted harness retains all attempts and state checks.

templates.title: Verify {domain} accessibility across interaction states
steps: Run configured automated checks for each required page and state through the trusted verifier.
Exercise keyboard navigation, dialogs, errors, and focus restoration.
Inspect zoom, reflow, contrast, motion, and touch behavior.
Record assistive-technology checks actually performed and those still missing.
Link every violation to a precise reproduction and owning frontend task.
acceptance: Zero automated violations is reported only from actual fresh output.
Untested states remain explicit release gaps.
validation: Reviewer independently reproduces selected findings and fixed interactions.

templates.title: Specify {domain} load and latency acceptance
inputs: Concrete domain request and browser paths
steps: Choose realistic records, payloads, actor mix, and concurrency increments.
Identify cold and warm scenarios and success/error classification.
Set disposable target, maximum duration, resource caps, and abort criteria.
Measure API p95, page load, throughput, errors, memory, and queue delay.
Plan recovery checks after load is removed.
acceptance: Capacity claims are limited to the measured environment and workload.
No public production target is exercised.
validation: Reviewer checks sample sizes, warmup, error inclusion, and reproducibility.

templates.title: Repair measured {domain} performance bottlenecks
inputs: Baseline and target under identical conditions
Accepted exact file/route/action breakdown from d_tasks; broad path scopes are an upper bound, not permission to rewrite unrelated files.
steps: Reproduce the measured bottleneck and identify its dominant cost.
Choose the smallest query, caching, batching, rendering, or resource fix.
Preserve authorization, freshness, ordering, and error semantics.
Compare before and after using the same workload and environment.
Run correctness and regression checks for the changed path.
acceptance: Optimization is justified by measured cost rather than speculation.
Cache changes cannot leak tenants or hide invalidation failures.
validation: Trusted measurements retain latency distribution and error counts.
Reviewer checks correctness under load and cold state.

templates.title: Verify {domain} retention, export, and erasure behavior
steps: Trace where the domain stores personal and sensitive data.
Specify and inspect authorized export and erasure behavior.
Identify retained financial, rights, audit, provider, and backup exceptions.
Verify cleanup and access revocation across derived stores and assets.
Record unsupported requests and policy questions explicitly.
acceptance: Deletion claims identify exact stores and explicit exceptions.
Technical verification is not represented as legal certification.
validation: Reviewer checks export isolation and erase ownership.
Trusted tests inspect durable post-request state.

templates.title: Independently review {domain} security changes and residual risks
inputs: Domain threat model and unresolved findings
steps: Review the actual diff and affected trust boundaries.
Reconcile each finding with mitigation and trusted test evidence.
Inspect new inputs, permissions, logs, dependencies, and side effects introduced by the fix.
Reproduce high-impact denial and replay cases through approved checks.
Return pass, fail, or unverified with concrete residual findings.
acceptance: No owner self-approval satisfies independent review.
Critical and high findings remain release blockers.
validation: Reviewer must reference exact changed paths and current source identity.
Narrative approval alone cannot override a failing security gate.

templates.title: Write accurate {domain} API and integration documentation
steps: Document request, response, authentication, permission, and error examples.
Explain pagination, idempotency, retries, timeouts, and callbacks.
Identify sandbox prerequisites and unsupported provider operations.
Cross-check every example against current types and actual handler behavior.
Write documentation proposals in the private task directory for reviewed placement.
acceptance: Examples do not contain secrets or invented successful responses.
Unsupported behavior is clearly labeled.
validation: Reviewer validates examples against the accepted contract and trusted tests.

templates.title: Write {domain} user guidance and recovery instructions
steps: Describe prerequisites and step-by-step user actions for each supported journey.
Explain visible success, pending, rejected, and unavailable states.
Document error recovery, cancellation, permissions, and support escalation.
Use actual labels and avoid promising unverified integrations.
Write proposed accessible guidance with source and evidence references.
acceptance: Instructions match current UI labels and real behavior.
A reader can distinguish a completed action from a pending request.
validation: Reviewer follows the instructions through the trusted browser scenario.

templates.title: Write {domain} operational diagnosis and recovery runbooks
steps: Map symptoms to logs, metrics, traces, and authoritative state checks.
Define safe diagnosis for unavailable providers, stuck jobs, stale data, and failed mutations.
Specify bounded retry, reconciliation, rollback, and escalation steps.
List required capabilities and prohibited production actions for this loop.
Record evidence needed to declare the incident resolved.
acceptance: Runbooks do not grant arbitrary production mutation authority.
Recovery requires state and user-outcome evidence, not only a healthy process.
validation: Reviewer walks a provider outage and interrupted mutation using the runbook.

templates.title: Reconcile {domain} criteria with trusted execution evidence
inputs: Criterion matrix and current source identity
Trusted gate results and raw artifacts
steps: Resolve every acceptance criterion to actual current evidence.
Mark proposed, unexecuted, skipped, stale, failed, and passing cases separately.
Check that tests exercise real required dependencies and durable outcomes.
Reopen criteria affected by later source changes.
Route each unresolved criterion to its concrete owner and next task.
deliverables: Exact failed and unverified criterion backlog
acceptance: Worker claims and test proposals cannot mark a criterion passed.
All required scenarios remain represented after retries or cycle exhaustion.
validation: Independent reviewer resolves the evidence references and samples authoritative outcomes.

templates.title: Prepare the {domain} release evidence packet
inputs: Domain acceptance matrix and documentation proposals
steps: Bind accepted work to exact source, policy, runtime, and artifact identity.
List all changed files, independent review results, and verification commands.
Include rollback, migration, provider, monitoring, and recovery prerequisites.
Record remaining blockers and release recommendation.
Hand the packet to the platform release matrix without merging or deploying.
acceptance: A completed packet is not a deployment or production-readiness claim.
Any required missing evidence produces NO-GO or unverified status.
validation: Reviewer reconciles packet entries with current trusted reports and source hashes.

templates.title: Reproduce a concrete {domain} defect before repair
inputs: Observed failed gate or user scenario
steps: Preserve the failing input, command, logs, and observable symptom.
Reduce the case while preserving the failed business invariant.
Determine whether the cause is product code, fixture, environment, provider, or missing capability.
Demonstrate the failure repeatedly or record why it is intermittent.
Assign a concrete repair hypothesis and regression scenario to the owning role.
acceptance: An environment blocker is not mislabeled as an application defect.
Root cause remains a hypothesis until controlled evidence supports it.
validation: Independent reviewer reruns the reproduction when capability is available.

templates.title: Review {domain} patch correctness and maintainability
steps: Inspect the actual diff and every changed call site.
Check business invariants, compatibility, error handling, and failure cleanup.
Look for unrelated changes, duplicate implementations, and hidden configuration dependencies.
Verify claimed tests exist as evidence rather than proposed prose.
Return actionable findings or a source-bound review conclusion.
acceptance: Approval refers to the actual candidate source hash.
Changes to protected validation are routed outside automatic repair.
validation: Reviewer checks at least the original defect and one adjacent regression risk.

templates.title: Evaluate {domain} repair effectiveness and update the next assignment
inputs: Attempt history and current failed criteria
steps: Compare the intended fix with actual gate and invariant outcomes.
Identify new regressions, repeated patches, unchanged failures, and wasted checks.
Record which hypothesis was disproved and what evidence is still missing.
Propose the next smallest task or escalation with a different investigation approach.
Preserve all requirements and thresholds while improving ordering or task precision.
acceptance: A failed attempt cannot improve readiness by relabeling evidence.
No-progress and repeated failures remain visible termination reasons.
validation: Reviewer compares the next task against the prior failed hypothesis and raw results.

templates.title: Specify and verify private admin access
inputs: Observed routes, admin entitlement checks and release evidence
steps: Identify the configured admin identity and authoritative role derivation without exposing credentials.
Enumerate all page, API, socket, download, worker trigger and registration entry points.
Require anonymous and non-admin denial where private launch access is required, including direct requests.
Specify login, MFA, session expiry, revocation and recovery acceptance with lockout recovery.
Document intentionally public static, health and owner-published sharing surfaces; prove none disclose private application data or confer account access.
deliverables: Source-linked findings and narrow patch or reviewable proposal
acceptance: Private access cannot be bypassed by hiding navigation only.
Admin access recovery and denial tests have real evidence.
validation: Trusted fixture tests admin success, anonymous denial, non-admin denial and expired/revoked sessions.

templates.title: Audit full admin feature entitlements
inputs: Observed routes, admin entitlement checks and release evidence
steps: Inventory feature, subscription, quota and plan checks across frontend, API and job handlers.
Map every admin workflow to required entitlements and identify artificial paywalls on the owner account.
Specify centrally derived admin entitlement behavior while preserving financial, provider and resource constraints.
Verify that request parameters or client state cannot confer admin capabilities.
Keep payment creation, refund and provider spending outcomes real and permission checked.
deliverables: Source-linked findings and narrow patch or reviewable proposal
acceptance: The administrator can reach every requested feature without buying a public plan.
Non-admin identity cannot obtain the same access by forged role or plan inputs.
validation: Positive admin and negative forged-role/paywall regression checks run against actual handlers.

templates.title: Assemble independent private-release decision
inputs: Observed routes, admin entitlement checks and release evidence
steps: Collect source-bound admin criteria and all twelve domain journey results.
Verify production build, actual startup, health, shutdown, persistence across restart and configured providers.
Require recoverable backups, restoration proof, monitoring and a tested rollback path.
Separate private-admin blockers from deferred public-launch work; never convert skipped integrations to passing.
Record GO only for the tested admin release when every required admin criterion has evidence; otherwise record exact blockers.
deliverables: Source-linked findings and narrow patch or reviewable proposal
acceptance: Private admin release and public general availability are reported separately.
No deployment is authorized by a task completion count.
validation: Run the trusted admin acceptance producer and final source-to-artifact validation.

templates.title: Exercise every admin action in {domain}
inputs: Observed routes, admin entitlement checks and release evidence
steps: Enumerate every admin-visible action and link it to an accepted scenario, actual route, handler and durable record.
Perform create/read/update/delete or the domain-equivalent workflow through the browser as the administrator.
Reload, sign out/in and restart the isolated runtime; confirm the result and uploaded artifacts survive.
Exercise invalid inputs, permission denial, interrupted requests, retries and provider failures.
Verify exports, collaboration, publishing and financial effects against their authoritative destination where applicable.
Record any missing integration or dead control as a blocker with the exact reproduction and owner.
deliverables: Source-linked findings and narrow patch or reviewable proposal
acceptance: All admin workflow outcomes are real, durable and observable.
Each required domain journey has positive, failure, reload and authorization evidence.
validation: Source-bound browser/API checks verify all four catalog journeys and every discovered admin control.

release_target.goal: The administrator can use every Max Booster domain end to end with durable real outcomes.
release_target.authorized_scope_change: I want Max Booster production grade enough for the admin account to run and use it in its entirety the ability to be used by everyone can wait
required: All twelve domain workflows remain in scope.
Private access is enforced at server endpoints as well as navigation.
Admin entitlements do not require purchasing a public plan; provider charges and financial authorization stay real.
Security, persistence, provider truthfulness, backup/restore and rollback remain required.
Current-source admin acceptance and later public-launch acceptance have separate decisions.
deferred: Public self-service registration and mass onboarding
General availability for every persona and subscription tier
Large-scale multiuser capacity and public growth experiments
release_target.planning_rule: Interpret every template for the admin-private release. Record deferred public work in a separate backlog without deleting it. Existing global coverage thresholds remain public-platform criteria; admin readiness requires complete critical-journey acceptance, not an invented coverage score.
